Subject: Reference design for Redwood connector - initial pack

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the call last week. Attached is our first-pass reference diagram for the connector between Aurum's orchestration layer and Redwood Private (encrypted VPC mode). The doc highlights our expected network flows, data classification rules, and a short list of success criteria for the validation run.

Primary asks:
- Quick review of the architecture for any obvious security/compatibility gaps
- Confirmation of supported auth flows (we called out OAuth2 + mutual TLS as a must)
- Rough estimate on a test-fleet (2–4 GPUs) that'll be sufficient for a 48-hour smoke run

I've included Asha (our solutions lead) on the thread. For attachments: aurum-reference-arch-v1.pdf and aurum-interop-test-plan.csv.

Best,
Samir

Hi Samir — thanks for the pack and the diagram. Quick notes from product/ops POV:

- High level looks reasonable. We'll need to confirm the mutual TLS handshake path through the customer-managed NAT; that can impact our HSM/KMS routing.
- OAuth2 with token exchange is supported; we recommend using short-lived tokens and our token-exchange endpoint for service-to-service calls.
- For a 48-hour smoke run using a canonical language model (50–100B), you should expect 2x A100 equivalent GPUs to be a safe lower bound; 4 GPUs for parallelized prompting at scale (Aurum test scenarios 2–4). I'll ask infra for a formal capacity estimate.

I'll schedule a 30-minute technical checkpoint with Karthik and Vivek tomorrow so we can walk the diagram and map out a validation checklist. Is 10am BST / 05:00 EDT workable for you?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com

Forwarding the annotated architecture and the start of our validation plan. See attached: aurum-reference-arch-v1.pdf (annotated by infra) and aurum-interop-test-plan.csv (with an added 'redwood_checks' column).

Key additions we made in the annotations:
- Explicitly call out the mutual TLS cert rotation timeline and who holds the intermediate CA (Aurum operations).
- Added a KV cache invalidation step to the test plan; this verifies prefix caching behavior across restarts.
- Added perf gate: 99th percentile tail latency under 350ms for single-conversation infer (seq len 512) in canary region.

Next steps:
1) Aurum to confirm CA holder and cert rotation cadence.
2) Redwood infra to provide a formal fleet estimate and an ephemeral test account. (Karthik to own.)
3) Book a 90-minute lab session for the smoke run the week of Sep 22 — Karthik/Vivek will lead.

- Lauren

Lauren / Samir — looping in some technical redlines from infra and reliability after a quick pass. I pasted the short checklist below and added delta actions inline.

Redlines / action items:
1) mTLS through customer NAT: need TCP passthrough on port 8443; Aurum to confirm firewall rule changes. (Aurum)
2) KMS integration: we need a test vector for envelope encryption; Aurum to provide a sample wrapped key or allow our test vector to be used. (Aurum)
3) Cache invalidation: add a deterministic key prefix to smoke tests so we can assert cache miss/hit behavior after redeploy. (Redwood)
4) Canary fallback: define the fallback model variant (smaller quantized variant) and the throttling policy during rollback. (Joint)

I also updated aurum-interop-test-plan.csv with an explicit perf profile and the exact cURL commands we will use for healthchecks. See attached: aurum-interop-test-plan.csv and aurum-ktp-checklist.xlsx.

I'll own the infra estimate — preliminary: 3x A100-equivalent for an exhaustive smoke run with parallel scenarios; can drop to 2 if Aurum serializes traffic during the run. I'll share a formal capacity sheet by Mon 15 Sep.

-karthik
